title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 4th draft of 'Analysis situs' (1986) Grothendieck axiomatises a point-free geometry of 'lieux' (places, figures, 'imaginaires'). A 'magma' M is a set of lieux with: an order ≤ (inclusion); a strong or interior inclusion X <̇ Y (rendered X <<° Y on the next page); and a symmetric, antireflexive disjointness relation X |∘| Y (also written |·|). He looks for a 'support function' X ↦ |X| from lieux to subsets of a space, ideally faithful, i.e. injective and order-reflecting. His closure notation for |X| is X̃. The previous page (Example 1) says: if the supports are definable through <̇, so that disjointness means 'no common strongly-contained lieu', then X ↦ Ouv(X), M ↦ 𝔉(M) gives a faithful support function. A margin note adds that this is a fully faithful functor.

Example 2 (this page). Take magmas built from pseudo-simplices and similar figures in a topological space X (or a modified space). For instance, those attached to a topological 'rope/string' (corde, ficelle), or more generally to any manifold, as in the preceding §. As far as the handwriting allows, the lieux are apparently not rich enough for disjointness to be recovered intrinsically in the Example 1 way. 'But all the same, the faithful support function with values in 𝔓(X) is ready-made!' Each figure simply has its underlying point set in X.

Example 3 (discrete/trivial magmas). Set X |∘| Y ⇔ X ≠ Y and X <̇ Y ⇔ X = Y. Then X |·| Y iff there is no Z with Z <̇ X and Z <̇ Y. This is exactly the situation of Example 1, where disjointness is defined from strong inclusion. Define |X| := X̃ = M_{≤X} = Ouv(X), the closure of X for the Alexandrov-type topology on M associated with ≤. This gives a faithful support function, with interior support |X|° = {X} for every X.

The next page goes on to define cosupp°(A) = {X : A |∘| X} and supp° = cosupp°∘cosupp°. This is the Galois closure, or 'double orthogonal', of the disjointness relation, i.e. the orthocomplementation closure familiar from orthogonality spaces and from regular-open / Boolean-algebra constructions.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. Example 3 is consistent: in the discrete magma ≤ and <̇ are presumably equality, so M_{≤X} = {X}, its closure and interior are both {X}, and 'X ≠ Y iff no Z equal to both' holds trivially.
Example 2 is only sketched. The claim about what the lieux fail to determine is not stated precisely in the legible text.

ideas.what: Point-free geometry: lieux with inclusion, strong inclusion and disjointness, realised by a faithful 'support function' into subsets of a space
ideas.modern_name: mereotopology / region-based topology (contact algebras, Region Connection Calculus), representation theorems for region structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead (1929), de Laguna, Tarski (geometry of solids), Clarke (1981), Randell–Cui–Cohn (1992), Düntsch–Vakarelov (contact algebras, 2000s)
ideas.where_published: Analysis situs notes (cote 156) unpublished; the theme of tame topology is only hinted at in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Defining disjointness from strong inclusion: X |·| Y iff no Z <̇ X, Z <̇ Y
ideas.modern_name: overlap/disjointness defined via common parts (classical mereology), as in Leśniewski / Leonard–Goodman

ideas.what: Discrete magma example, with support given by closure in the Alexandrov topology of ≤
ideas.modern_name: Alexandrov (specialisation-order) topology; trivial model of an orthogonality space

ideas.what: Pseudo-simplices and figures in a space or manifold as a magma with ready-made point-set support
ideas.modern_name: concrete region models (e.g. polyhedral or semialgebraic regions) of mereotopology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pratt-Hartmann and others for polygonal/polyhedral mereotopology

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 'magma of lieux' framework closely parallels mereotopology and region connection calculi developed independently in philosophy/AI/logic. The faithful support function corresponds to a representation theorem, and the next page's double-orthogonal supp° matches orthogonality-space closure. This link does not appear in the literature on either side.
missed.quote: Mais pourtant, la fonction support fidèle à valeurs dans 𝔓(X) est toute trouvée!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could situate Grothendieck's late foundational work on 'analysis situs' within mereotopology and point-free topology, which have well-developed representation theory. That would help in evaluating whether his drafts contain anything beyond those theories.

deep.surprise_reason: The page consists of elementary examples, one trivial (discrete magmas) and one only sketched. The broader unpublished program and its unremarked parallel with mereotopology are mildly interesting, but nothing on this page is a substantive new result.
transcription_corrections: 'la fonction [?] fait à valeurs dans $\not\exists(X)$ [?] toutes [?]!' should read roughly 'la fonction support fidèle [?] à valeurs dans $\mathfrak{P}(X)$ est toute trouvée!'.
'on ont [-que-] donc que' is better read 'on a donc que'.
In Example 2, 'de lieux suffisants pour un [?] des disjoints' is very uncertain; it seems to say the lieux are not sufficient to define disjointness intrinsically.
